{"statements": {"L1.1": {"established": "yes", "quote": "Every move strictly decreases $(T,c)$. Since the lexicographic order on
$\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$ has no infinite strictly decreasing chain, only finitely many
moves are possible. Thus the process always stops. A move is possible exactly when
$c\ge2$, so at termination $c\le1$.", "note": "Lex monovariant covers both cases; "at least one >1" proved via positive G_p invariant, non-circular."}, "L1.2": {"established": "yes", "quote": "$$\gcd\bigl(\min(\alpha,\beta),\,|\alpha-\beta|\bigr)=\gcd(\alpha,\beta-\alpha)=\gcd(\alpha,\beta)$$
by Euclid's identity. Therefore the gcd of the two touched exponents is unchanged,
hence the gcd of the *entire* multiset of $p$-exponents — i.e. $G_p$ — is
unchanged.", "note": "WLOG plus stated gcd(0,x)=x convention handles equal and zero valuations; yields v_p(M)=G_p."}}, "S_ref": 2, "notes": "Move rewritten to (min, |diff|) explicitly; explicit M = prod p^{gcd_i v_p(a_i)} stated. Termination via well-founded lex pair (T,c), survivor existence via positive invariant rather than the "never two 1s" route, which is equivalent. Numerical checks clearly labeled as non-proof."}
